_readme: Approved inline <script> blocks for this site's Content-Security-Policy.
scripts/build-security-headers.js hashes every inline script on every page
(all the top-level HTML files plus every generated products/*.html) and
refuses to build if it finds one that is not listed here. Without that
check the generator re-hashed whatever it found on each deploy, so any
script that reached a page -- including text typed into the CMS at /admin
and interpolated into the Tawk.to snippet by build-site-data.js -- was
automatically allowlisted by the very policy meant to contain it. That is
findings C-4 and H-13 in docs/AUDIT-2026-09-01.md.
WHEN THE BUILD FAILS ON A NEW HASH: read the script it prints. Confirm
line by line that it is a change you or a colleague made on purpose. Only
then add its hash below, with a note saying what the script does and which
file emits it, in the same commit as the change itself. Never paste in a
hash to make a red build go green.
A hash listed here that matches nothing on the site is reported as stale
on every build and is left out of the emitted CSP; delete it once you are
sure the script is gone for good.

sha256-Wmlc/Lumj50wOdax6AEbaQv0zXK/9D0NZ.what: No-flash theme init: reads the yl-theme preference and sets data-theme before first paint.

sha256-X8kUvpVWVbaRRvoM1l6EpaLEU/5DbGswO.what: Tawk.to live-chat loader, deferred. Loads the widget SDK on the visitor's first pointerdown/keydown/scroll/touchstart, never on a timer: an idle-timeout fallback made the widget iframe land with no user input and register as a 0.047 layout shift on every page (2026-09-02). The two IDs still come from content.json via scripts/build-site-data.js, so this hash still changes whenever they change in /admin. Rehashed 2026-09-02 (live audit M-1): the loader used to call s1.setAttribute("crossorigin", "*") -- not a value the enumerated attribute accepts, so the browser fell back to the anonymous state and made a CORS-mode fetch out of a request that needs no CORS, with no integrity hash to justify it. The diff was reviewed line by line before this hash was written down: it is that one line deleted and nothing else, so the snippet stays byte-identical everywhere it is emitted and one hash keeps covering every page that carries it.

sha256-gUmq6gOoZ76O8R+C9JLLJzm46Aj4WygKv.what: Speculation-rules JSON that main.js builds at runtime (JSON.stringify of its prerender/prefetch rules object) and appends as <script type="speculationrules">. It is never present in the static HTML, so the page scan cannot see it; 'runtime: true' keeps it in the emitted CSP as belt-and-braces beside the 'inline-speculation-rules' keyword. If the rules object in main.js changes, recompute this hash from JSON.stringify(rules).
sha256-gUmq6gOoZ76O8R+C9JLLJzm46Aj4WygKv.emittedBy: assets/js/main.js (speculation rules block, appended to <body> at runtime)
